tossups.text: In this decade, Black servicemen turned on their superiors during the Townsville Mutiny. The serial killer Eddie Leonski, known as the "Brownout Strangler," was active in this decade and had previously served at Melbourne's Camp Pell. In this decade, soldiers who fought the so-called "Battle of Brisbane" were described as "over-paid, over-sexed, and over here." In this decade, "the strivers, the planners, the ambitious ones" were praised in the "Forgotten People" speech. In this decade, Papua New Guinean laborers along the Kokoda Track were given the nickname "fuzzy-wuzzy angels." In this decade, John Curtin succeeded Robert Menzies as prime minister, and Australia faced its worst domestic attack when 242 planes bombed Darwin. For 10 points, name this decade during which Australia fought in World War II.

A Georg Nicolaus study compares Jung's concept of individuation with this thinker's early notion of "the person." This anarchist drew upon Tolstoy and his faith to claim that "the kingdom of God is anarchy" in his late book Slavery and Freedom. This thinker founded the Academy of Spiritual Culture during a crusade in which he described the ruling ideology of his home country as perpetrating the "New Dark Ages." In a 1916 book, this thinker asserted that the cult of holiness in Christianity should coexist with the cult of the creative genius, since the point of existence isn't to be redeemed by God but instead to attempt to create like Him. This thinker fled the Soviet Union after being tortured by the Cheka, settling in Berlin and then Paris. Though in his time he wrote an early account of the philosophy of love in The Meaning of the Creative Act, today he is probably best remembered for writing an infamous footnote in which he claimed "this was revealed to me in a dream." For 10 points, name this Russian Christian Existentialist philosopher.

The nomadic Toubou [too-boo] people populate the Tibesti Mountains in this larger region. The Ayir Massif of this region includes a recent tourist destination of hills featuring cipollino marble outcroppings called the Blue Mountains. Much of the central region of this area is dominated by the Grand Erg Oriental, a massive sand sea. The Qattara Depression lies east of the Siwa Oasis in this large arid location. Bordered on the south by a transitional zone called the Sahel is, for 10 points, what massive hot desert comprising much of North Africa?

A running theme in one of this author's novel series is the day November 25th, 1970, on which another author died. One novel in that series by this author sees "The Boss" tell its protagonist, whose girlfriend has magical ears, about an animal with a star shaped birthmark on its head. That trilogy by this author which revolves around "The Rat" includes the novels Hear the Wind Sing and Pinball, 1973. The protagonist of one of this author's novels releases a firefly from his rooftop that he had received from his roommate, the geography major Storm Trooper. That novel by this author revolves around Toru Watanabe's love triangle with the depressive Naoko and the vivacious Midori, and is named after a Beatles song. For 10 points, name this author of A Wild Sheep Chase and Norwegian Wood.

Descriptive answer acceptable In one of these conflicts, a man called "Jack of the Feather" by his enemies unsuccessfully tried to stop the founding of the town of Henricus. The second of these events opened with a massacre that killed 1/3 of one side's population. Ophecanough was the weroance of one side during the last two of these conflicts. The boundaries established by the final of these wars were reworked in the Treaty of Middle Plantation. The first of these conflicts was fueled by the violent means by which Lord De La Warr ended the Starving Time. For 10 points, these were what series of early 17th century conflicts between the English settlers of Virginia and a group of Native American tribes led by Pocahontas' father?

Edward Bulwer-Lytton urged the author of this novel to change its ending, resulting in an episode set eleven years after the main action in which two characters join hands in a garden. In one scene from this novel, the protagonist's sister is viciously attacked by Dolge Orlick. One location in this novel takes its name from a Latin word meaning "enough" and is called Satis House; the resident of that house wears only one shoe and keeps all the clocks at eight forty in memory of her abandonment at the altar by Compeyson. This novel's protagonist befriends Herbert Pocket in London, but he is disappointed when he discovers that Bentley Drummle has married his beloved Estella. This novel's main character is surprised to discover that his benefactor is the convict Abel Magwitch. For 10 points, name this novel about Pip by Charles Dickens.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for water absorption. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this colon-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The colon is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in water absorption.

tossups.text: The protagonist of this novel stumbles into a forest after throwing a pinecone at a squirrel. During this novel, the protagonist fights over a flag with Tom Wilson, and abandons a "tattered soldier" who has been shot twice. The protagonist of this novel gains bravery after replacing Jim Conklin as the flag bearer. For 10 points, name this Civil War novel about Henry Fleming, written by Stephen Crane.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for cerebral cortex lobes. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cerebrum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cerebrum is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in cerebral cortex lobes.

tossups.text: This man stated that "it takes more than that to kill a bull moose" during a speech after he was shot. After resigning as Assistant Secretary of the Navy, this man fought at the Battle of San Juan Hill with the Rough Riders during the Spanish-American War. For 10 points, name this trustbusting president and successor to William McKinley, who lends his name to a stuffed toy bear.

One church in this city depicts the ten martyrs of the twentieth century, while another church's "Warrant Design" is in the shape of a Latin cross. That building's 365-foot dome has a continuous colonnade with a niche in every fourth opening. A Norman-Foster designed skyscraper in this city has bands of light and dark glass, is known as the Gherkin, and is at 30 St. Mary's Axe. This city's tallest building is a 95-story glass skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano, the Shard. For 10 points, name this city where Christopher Wren rebuilt St. Paul's Cathedral after a "great" 1666 fire.

Max Weber [vay-ber] argued that in this kind of economy, earning money glorified God. This kind of economy relies on the free market to help generate profit from investments. For 10 points, name this kind of economy that emphasizes private property and working for wages, such as in the United States.
acceptableAnswers: accept free market economy before mentioned

tossups.text: All members of the Rhacodactylus genus are found in this territory, including the world's largest gecko. The Amborella plant genus native to this territory was one of the first to branch off from the angiosperms. A family of flightless birds endemic to this territory possess unique "corns" covering their nostrils, can use their wings to help them climb trees, and are called kagus. A crow found in this territory has been observed trimming twigs off branches to make them better suited for probing anthills in an unusual example of avian tool manufacture. This territory will hold an independence referendum in November 2018 in accordance with an agreement with its native Kanak people. For 10 points, name this French overseas territory with its capital at Noumea.

With Lebesgue, this man's name denotes a lemma which states that if a function oscillates rapidly about zero, its integral will be small. With Cauchy, his name describes a set of equations necessary for a complex function to be holomorphic, and his namesake surface is a one-dimensional complex manifold. This man may be most famous for formulating one of the most well known unsolved problems in mathematics - whether the real part of any nontrivial zero of his eponymous zeta function has real part one-half. For 10 points, name this German mathematician whose namesake sums also approach his namesake integral.

Mohammad Reza Pahlavi was forced to flee this country in the wake of its 1979 Islamic Revolution. Jimmy Carter lost the Election of 1980 partially due to the capture of fifty-two American diplomats in a "hostage crisis" named for this country. This country was invaded by neighboring Iraq to limit the power of its Shia majority. The rise of Ayatollah Khomeini in this country ended the Persian monarchy. For 10 points, name this country where a US embassy was attacked in Tehran.

This man was accused of falsifying papers about his adoption by Lucius Quietus. This leader, who withdrew the army from Mesopotamia, went on a grand tour away from his villa at Tivoli and deified a boy who drowned in the Nile named Antinous. Rabbi Akiva supported Simon Bar Kochba's Jewish revolt against this first bearded Roman emperor, who negotiated a peace with Parthia in AD 121 and had the Parthenon rebuilt before Antoninus Pius succeeded him. For 10 points, name this successor to Trajan, a so-called Good Emperor who had a ditch dug in front of his namesake defensive "wall" in Britain.

Deriving this function for a Cobb-Douglas utility function sometimes relies on the Lagrange approach. The Slutsky equation relates changes between two types of this function, one that maximizes utility, and another that minimizes expenditure. Those two types of this function are Marshallian and Hicksian, respectively. The cross price elasticity of this quantity is positive for substitutes and negative for complements. This quantity and price are negatively correlated, since when price rises, this quantity typically decreases. For 10 points, name this economic concept which is often paired with supply.

This work's narrator eats a small scroll, which tastes sweet but is bitter in his stomach. In this book, 144,000 people are sealed as servants of God. This Biblical book, which is addressed to seven churches, describes the sounding of seven trumpets and the opening of seven seals, the first four of which are accompanied by horsemen. For 10 points, identify this last book of the New Testament, which describes the end of the world.

The structure of some objects containing this substance was investigated by Navaroo, Frenk, and White using N-body simulations. Valentjin and van der Werf suggested that molecular hydrogen accounts for most of this substance. Douglas Clowe "proved" its existence while studying the Bullet Cluster and gravitational lensing effects. This substance may be composed of massive compact halo objects or weakly interacting massive particles. This mostly non-baryonic substance is divided into warm, hot and cold types. For 10 points, name this hypothetical substance that, along with dark energy, makes up around eighty-five percent of the mass of the universe.

This body of water was refilled by the Zanclean flood over five million years ago, ending the Messinian salinity crisis. The Barbary Coast was along this body of water, which lies west of the Levant and south of Asia Minor. The Strait of Gibraltar separates this sea from the Atlantic Ocean, and its Aegean and Adriatic Seas were considered part of "the Great Sea" by the ancient Greeks and Romans. For 10 points, name this sea that separates Europe and Africa.

parts.text: Swashbuckler Jean Lafitte led his band of Baratarian privateers in fighting for the American cause at this battle in which the British general Edward Pakenham was defeated.

American disgust toward paying tribute money to the Barbary pirates led to the Pasha of this Barbary state to declare war on the United States in 1801. American troops under Preble and Decatur led a naval blockade of its harbor during the war.

In 1873, Joseph Fry and 52 other crew and passengers were executed as pirates after this ship was captured by the Spanish, causing a strain in Spanish-American relations. This ship had been carrying arms to rebelling Cubans while flying the American flag.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about pirates in American history, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this husband of Fatima.
Ali is looked upon as the first imam in this sect of Islam popular in Iran and Iraq.
Ali's caliphate was marred by this civil war following the assassination of Uthman, which ended with his own assassination.

bonuses.leadin: His followers argue for his importance based on the Hadiths of the Two Weighty Things and of the Pond of Kumm. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this third largest city in the world, and capital of the Sindh province. It is regularly ranked as one of the most unlivable cities in the world due to poor sanitation and crime.
Karachi is the largest city in this country, which currently disputes ownership over the Kashmir region with its eastern neighbor, India. Its capital is Islamabad.

This pass is a major tourist destination in Pakistan, located by the city of Peshawar and near the border with Afghanistan. It was a vital route on the Silk Road and was used by invaders to reach the Indian subcontinent.

bonuses.leadin: This city is the site of Empress Market and the Port of Bin Qasim. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this "poet of the American Revolution," best known for "The Indian Burying-Ground."
Freneau concludes "The space between is but an hour, The frail duration of a flower" in this poem about a "fair flower, that dost so comely grow."
Several of Freneau's poems were published in Selections from American Poets, an anthology published by this editor of the New York Evening Post who wrote "Thanatopsis" and "To a Waterfowl."

bonuses.leadin: He collaborated with Hugh Henry Brackenridge on the satire Father Bombo's Pilgrimage to Mecca, one of the earliest American novels. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this most important Greek colony in Libya, often known as the "Athens of Africa." Plutarch described how one of its noblewomen, Aretaphilia, overthrew the tyrant Nicocrates in On the Virtues of Women.

Eratosthenes of Cyrene was the first person to have calculated this value with accuracy. Columbus' inaccurate ideas about this value led him to think he could reach India quickly by sailing across the Atlantic Ocean.

A sculpture of this deity unearthed at Cyrene in 1913 was returned to Libya by Italy in 2008. Another sculpture of this deity was unearthed in the Aegean in 1920 and depicted in Pablo Picasso's Hallucinogenic Toreador.

bonuses.leadin: A Roman province named for this city oddly included Crete. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel in which Meursault shoots an Arab five times on a beach.
The Stranger was written by this French novelist of works such as The Plague and The Fall. He received the 1957 Nobel Prize in Literature.
Six of Camus' short stories are collected in this volume, including a story in which an engineer named d'Arrast goes to a town in Brazil whose inhabitants celebrate the miracle of a "growing stone".

bonuses.leadin: In this novel, the examining magistrate of a murder case brandishes a crucifix at the protagonist and asks if he believes in God, to which the protagonist replies "no". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with heart valves and their functions.
What is the main function of the atrium in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to heart valves and their functions.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this Russian author, who also wrote novels like Notes from the Underground and The Idiot, and who wrote about Ivan, Alexei, and Dmitri in The Brothers Karamazov.
Raskolnikov eventually confesses to murdering a pawnbroker and her sister and is exiled to Siberia in this novel by Dostoevsky.

Raskolnikov commits his crime in this Russian city on the Neva River. Alexander Pushkin wrote The Bronze Horseman about a statue of Peter the Great in this city, which has also been called Petrograd and Leningrad.

bonuses.leadin: In a novel by this author, investigator Porfiry Petrovich and Sonya Marmeladova try to persuade Raskolnikov to confess to the murders he has committed. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with sweat glands.
What is the main function of the hair follicle in the integumentary system?
Name another component of the integumentary system related to sweat glands.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human integumentary system.

parts.text: The 12th Amendment changed the procedure by which this body determines the winner of presidential and vice presidential elections.
The 23rd Amendment doesn't qualify as "lesser-known" in this geographic location, whose residents were given the right to vote in presidential elections by the amendment.
This amendment, ratified in just over three months in 1971, changed the voting age to eighteen years old.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about lesser-known Constitutional amendments.

parts.text: Name this Henrik Ibsen play, which premiered in modern-day Oslo in 1876. The aforementioned music was compiled into two popular suites.
This Norwegian composer of the Holberg Suite and a collection of Lyric Pieces for piano wrote the incidental music for Peer Gynt.

One of Grieg's Lyric Pieces celebrates one of these events "at Troldhaugen." A march from Felix Mendelssohn's incidental music to A Midsummer Night's Dream precedes one of these events between Titania and Oberon, the faerie king and queen.

bonuses.leadin: Incidental music to this play includes the pieces "Morning Mood," "Anitra's Dance," "Solvieg's Song," and "In the Hall of the Mountain King." For 10 points each,

parts.text: These constructs are the smallest segmental units of sound that form meaningful distinctions.

This is the set of changes in pronunciation that took place as Proto-Indo-European developed into Proto-Germanic languages, for example, as p changed to f and d changed to t. It is elaborated by the elder of two brothers who also collected some Children's and Household Tales.

This is the major change in the pronunciation of the English language that took place between 1350 and 1500 and is the reason for peculiarities in English spelling; as a result of it, "time" [pronounced TEAM] became "time" [regular pronunciation], "feet" [FATE] became "feet", and so on.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some linguistics concepts related to sounds, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this region of the EM spectrum. Cavity magnetrons produce radiation in this region which can then be used to excite water molecules.
The emissions of Townes' ammonia maser are caused by a lone pair undergoing this classically forbidden process in which a particle penetrates a potential barrier without the energy needed to do so.

Instead of a maser, a circuit containing one of these diodes can be used as a microwave oscillator. These solid-state diodes, also called tunnel diodes, exhibit negative differential resistance due to a heavily doped P-N junction.

bonuses.leadin: A predecessor of the laser invented by Charles Townes produces emissions in this region of the electromagnetic spectrum using umbrella inversion. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these constructs. Unlike vectors, these constructs become their negatives under a full rotation.
Dirac spinors are used to describe fundamental particles of this type. These particles' wavefunctions are antisymmetric under exchange.

Because spinors must be rotated twice to return to their original orientation, one can think of spinors as rotating along one of these shapes. These non-orientable shapes can be made by putting a twist in a strip of paper.

bonuses.leadin: Solutions to the Dirac equation can be interpreted as the product of one of these constructs and a plane wave. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Rafael Trujillo, the dictator of this country, ordered a massacre of thousands of people depending on how they pronounced perejil, the word for parsley. This country shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.

The United Fruit Company killed possibly thousands of striking workers in a massacre named after this fruit. Chiquita, the successor to the United Fruit Company, mainly sells this curved yellow fruit.

People from this country captured during the Battle of Mier were executed in the Black Bean episode, where people had to select beans blindfolded, and would be executed if they selected a black bean. The earlier Goliad massacre occurred in this country.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about massacres named after food, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Rome's first king and legendary founder was this man. This man murdered his twin brother, Remus.
One of Rome's earliest rivals was this other Italian civilization. This civilization's most important city was Veii, which was conquered by Marcus Furius Camillus.

Rome was able to take control of Southern Italy after defeating this ruler at the Battle of Beneventum. This ruler used war elephants during his campaigns including the Battle of Argos, where this ruler was killed.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer the following about the rise of Rome.

parts.text: Name this type of good that is neither excludable nor rival, an example of which includes a tornado siren. These differ from common goods as common goods are rivalrous.
An example of market failure that can arise from public goods is this problem, in which actors either pay less than their fair share of a public good's costs or benefit more than their fair share.

This economist described knowledge as a "global public good." This Nobel laureate is best known for his work in information asymmetry and published the works Globalization and its Discontents and Making Globalization Work.

bonuses.leadin: A Lindahl equilibrium is a situation in which individuals pay for the marginal benefits they reap from these entities. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Hobbes is best known for this work, named for a biblical monster, that advocates commonwealths be ruled by absolute sovereigns -- that is, by monarchs -- who could prevent mankind from falling into a war of all against all.
Hobbes initially wrote Leviathan in English, but soon translated it into this language, where the phrase "war of all against all" became "bellum omnium contra omnes."
Hobbes also translated this ancient Greek author's History of the Peloponnesian War into English.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, give the following about the writings of Thomas Hobbes.

parts.text: Name this form of heavy metal poisoning that affects children who live in old houses with chipped paint.
Lead poisoning causes "basophilic stippling" of red blood cells by inhibiting the degradation of this type of nucleic acid, which makes up a 60S "large" subunit and 40S "small" subunit in eukaryotes.
By interfering with the synthesis of PBG, lead disrupts this biochemical pathway, whose committed step is the condensation of glycine with succinyl CoA to form delta-aminolevulinic acid.
acceptableAnswers: accept any answers that indicate making heme

bonuses.leadin: A grey-blue streak on the gums called a Burton line appears in this condition, mild cases of which are treated with the orally-administered succimer rather than calcium EDTA. For 10 points each:

parts.text: A 2015 New Yorker article detailed the coming destruction of Oregon and British Columbia due to an imminent earthquake in this subduction zone, named for a northwestern mountain range.
A series of enormous eruptions occurring over millions of years have originated from the supervolcano in this US national park, mostly found in Wyoming.
The San Andreas fault is projected to cause the separation of this currently continental American state from the mainland, forming an island that could travel north to Alaska.

bonuses.leadin: The end is nigh! Identify some future disasters in North America for 10 points each.
